head.title: Apache Axis2 OpenAPI Advanced Enterprise User Guide

body.h1: Apache Axis2 OpenAPI Advanced Enterprise User Guide
body.p: Enterprise-Grade OpenAPI Integration - This advanced guide covers the OpenAPI capabilities introduced in Axis2 2.0.1: configuration through properties files and system properties, security schemes in the generated specification, Swagger UI customization, the OpenApiCustomizer post-processing interface, and resource filtering.

Anything not covered by the configuration properties listed below (OAuth2 and API key security schemes, extra servers, tags, examples and extensions) is done programmatically with an OpenApiCustomizer. The OpenAPI module does not read environment variables.

This guide focuses on modern enterprise patterns including Bearer token authentication, OAuth2 integration, microservices architectures, cloud-native deployments, and developer-first API design principles. All examples use contemporary security and architectural patterns.
For legacy system integration patterns, see the Basic OpenAPI User Guide.
Axis2's OpenAPI integration represents a complete enterprise-grade solution for REST API development, documentation, and management. Unlike basic API documentation tools, this system provides:

ul.li: Configuration: openapi.* properties loaded from classpath properties files and system properties
Security Schemes: a JWT Bearer scheme by default; OAuth2, API keys and others added with a customizer
Developer Experience: Swagger UI with display options set through SwaggerUiConfig
Extensibility: OpenAPI customizer interface for post-processing and enhancements
Filtering: include or exclude resource packages, services, operations and routes
Container-ready: configuration through a mounted properties file or JVM system properties

body.p: This guide assumes familiarity with modern REST API design, OAuth2/JWT authentication, and enterprise development patterns. All examples follow contemporary security and architectural practices.
The Axis2 OpenAPI module reads its configuration from several sources, designed for enterprise deployment scenarios.
Configuration is loaded from the following sources; a later source overrides an earlier one (lowest precedence first):

ol.li: Module Parameters - title, version, description, prettyPrint, supportSwaggerUi and propertiesFile in the module's module.xml

Properties Files - openapi.properties on the classpath, the file named by the propertiesFile module parameter, and META-INF/openapi.properties, WEB-INF/openapi.properties or openapi-config.properties if present
System Properties - JVM system properties with the same openapi.* keys (highest precedence)

body.p: Create openapi.properties in your classpath. These are all the supported keys:
body.pre:
# API Information openapi.title=Financial Services API openapi.description=Enterprise financial services with comprehensive security openapi.version=2.1.0 openapi.contact.name=API Team openapi.contact.email=api-team@company.com openapi.contact.url=https://company.com/api-docs openapi.license.name=Commercial License openapi.license.url=https://company.com/license openapi.termsOfServiceUrl=https://company.com/terms
# Absolute URL for servers[].url (a relative URL is published by default) openapi.serverBaseUrl=https://api.company.com/axis2
# Resource Filtering openapi.readAllResources=false openapi.resourcePackages=com.company.api.v2,com.company.services openapi.ignoredRoutes=/internal/.*,/health,/metrics openapi.ignoredServices=AdminService,InternalService openapi.ignoredOperations=TradeService/debugDump,ping
# Swagger UI openapi.swaggerUi.enabled=true openapi.swaggerUi.version=5.32.13 # Only needed when openapi.swaggerUi.version is not the default: # openapi.swaggerUi.integrity.bundle=sha384-... # openapi.swaggerUi.integrity.standalonePreset=sha384-...
# Output openapi.prettyPrint=false openapi.useContextBasedConfig=false
body.p: Swagger UI is loaded from a CDN. For the default version the page pins Subresource Integrity hashes; if you choose another version, supply its hashes with the two openapi.swaggerUi.integrity.* keys, otherwise the page still renders but logs a warning that integrity is not enforced.
Override any setting with JVM system properties:
body.pre: java -Dopenapi.title="Development API" \ -Dopenapi.swaggerUi.enabled=true \ -jar your-application.jar
body.p: The generated specification can describe modern authentication patterns including OAuth2, JWT Bearer tokens and API keys. Axis2 documents these schemes; validating tokens remains the job of your service or of a security layer in front of it.

Modern REST APIs use Bearer token authentication. The generated specification declares an HTTP bearer security scheme named bearerAuth by default, so operations can reference it directly. To set bearerFormat or change the description, use a customizer (see Programmatic Security Configuration).

An OAuth2 security scheme, with its authorization and token URLs and scopes, is added to the specification programmatically; see Programmatic Security Configuration for a complete oauth2 scheme.
OAuth2 service implementation:
API key schemes (for example an X-API-Key header) are likewise declared with a customizer; the apiKeyAuth scheme in Programmatic Security Configuration shows one.
Service with API key authentication:
The specification can declare multiple simultaneous security schemes. Apart from the default bearerAuth scheme, they are configured in code.
Security setup using the OpenApiCustomizer interface:
Register the customizer on the module's configuration once the OpenAPI module has been initialized, for example from your application's startup code:
body.pre: OpenApiConfiguration config = OpenApiModule.getConfiguration(configContext); config.setCustomizer(new SecuritySchemeCustomizer());
body.p: Only one customizer is active at a time; to apply several, call them from a single customizer.
The OpenAPI module provides SwaggerUI customization capabilities for enterprise branding and functionality.

Only openapi.swaggerUi.enabled, openapi.swaggerUi.version and the two openapi.swaggerUi.integrity.* keys are read from properties (see Properties File Configuration). The display options are set in code on the module's SwaggerUiConfig:

The OpenApiCustomizer interface provides powerful post-processing capabilities for advanced OpenAPI specification enhancement.
Register it with OpenApiModule.getConfiguration(configContext).setCustomizer(...), as shown in Programmatic Security Configuration.
Resource filtering capabilities for large-scale enterprise APIs.
body.pre:
# Resource filtering configuration openapi.readAllResources=false
# Package-based filtering openapi.resourcePackages=com.company.api.v2,com.company.services.financial,com.company.auth
# Route exclusion patterns openapi.ignoredRoutes=/internal/.*,/admin/.*,/health,/metrics,/actuator/.*
# Service and operation exclusion openapi.ignoredServices=AdminService,MonitoringService openapi.ignoredOperations=TradeService/debugDump,ping
body.p: System services (such as Version and any service whose name contains AdminService) are excluded automatically.

body.h3: Financial Trading API with Bearer Authentication
body.p: Enterprise-grade performance optimization and monitoring capabilities for production deployments.

The OpenAPI module has no performance properties of its own. The specification responses carry a Cache-Control max-age of five minutes and static Swagger UI resources one of 24 hours, so a reverse proxy or CDN can cache them. Response compression, connection pooling and timeouts are configured in the servlet container or proxy.
Configuration and deployment patterns for cloud-native and containerized environments.
body.pre:
# Dockerfile FROM tomcat:11.0-jdk21
# OpenAPI settings are read from system properties (not environment variables) ENV JAVA_OPTS="-Dopenapi.swaggerUi.enabled=false -Dopenapi.resourcePackages=com.company.api.v2"
# Copy application; openapi.properties in Tomcat's lib directory is on the classpath COPY target/financial-api.war /usr/local/tomcat/webapps/ COPY config/openapi-production.properties /usr/local/tomcat/lib/openapi.properties
EXPOSE 8080 CMD ["catalina.sh", "run"]

apiVersion: v1 kind: ConfigMap metadata: name: openapi-config data: openapi.properties: | openapi.title=Financial Services API openapi.version=2.1.0 openapi.serverBaseUrl=https://api.company.com/axis2 openapi.swaggerUi.enabled=false --- apiVersion: apps/v1 kind: Deployment metadata: name: financial-api spec: replicas: 3 selector: matchLabels: app: financial-api template: metadata: labels: app: financial-api spec: containers: - name: api image: company/financial-api:2.1.0 ports: - containerPort: 8080 env: - name: JAVA_OPTS value: "-Dopenapi.title=Production-Financial-API" volumeMounts: - name: openapi-config mountPath: /usr/local/tomcat/lib/openapi.properties subPath: openapi.properties livenessProbe: httpGet: path: /health port: 8080 initialDelaySeconds: 30 periodSeconds: 10 readinessProbe: httpGet: path: /openapi.json port: 8080 initialDelaySeconds: 5 periodSeconds: 5 volumes: - name: openapi-config configMap: name: openapi-config
body.p: Comprehensive security guidelines for production OpenAPI deployments.

ul.li: ✓ JWT Token Validation: Implement proper JWT signature verification and expiration checking
✓ OAuth2 PKCE: Enforce PKCE for public clients and authorization code flows
✓ CORS Configuration: The specification endpoints send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *; restrict origins at the proxy or container if you need to
✓ Rate Limiting: Implement rate limiting per API key/user to prevent abuse
✓ Input Validation: Validate all request parameters against OpenAPI schemas
✓ HTTPS Only: Enforce HTTPS for all API endpoints and disable HTTP
✓ Security Headers: Include security headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options)
✓ API Key Rotation: Implement regular API key rotation policies
✓ Audit Logging: Log all API access and authentication events
✓ SwaggerUI Security: Disable SwaggerUI in production or restrict access

body.p: The OpenAPI module's own security-relevant settings are few:
body.pre:
# Disable SwaggerUI in production openapi.swaggerUi.enabled=false
# Publish a fixed absolute server URL instead of a relative one openapi.serverBaseUrl=https://api.company.com/axis2
body.p: HTTPS enforcement, HSTS, CORS restrictions, rate limiting and audit logging are not OpenAPI module settings; configure them in the servlet container, a servlet filter or the reverse proxy. The Swagger UI page sets its own Content-Security-Policy with a per-request nonce, and loads the default Swagger UI version with Subresource Integrity.
Common issues and advanced configuration scenarios for enterprise deployments.

ul.li: Configuration Precedence: System properties override properties files, which override module.xml parameters; environment variables are not read
Security Scheme Validation: Ensure OAuth2 endpoints are accessible and properly configured
Resource Filtering: Verify package names and class paths are correct
Memory Usage: Monitor memory usage with large OpenAPI specifications
Performance: Let a proxy or CDN cache the specification responses, which carry a Cache-Control max-age

body.pre: # Enable debug logging for the OpenAPI module (log4j2 example) <Logger name="org.apache.axis2.openapi" level="debug"/>
body.p: At startup the module logs the configuration sources it loaded (for example "Loaded OpenAPI configuration from: openapi.properties") and the resulting configuration.
For comprehensive support and advanced enterprise deployment scenarios, contact the Apache Axis2 development team or consult the Basic OpenAPI User Guide for fundamental concepts.

This advanced guide demonstrates the full enterprise capabilities of Axis2's OpenAPI integration. The system provides the flexibility and power needed for modern enterprise API development while maintaining the reliability and performance expected in production environments.
